extracted.intended_audience: Organ procurement organizations (OPOs/IOPOs), transplant hospitals, hospital finance and compliance staff, Medicare contractors/auditors, and CAHs
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and proposed codification of Medicare reasonable-cost principles covering allowable/unallowable education, travel, meals, cost-allocation methods, and appeals procedures for providers (with special focus on OPOs/IOPOs, transplant hospitals, and CAHs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable OPO‑sponsored seminars for OPO staff (CE credits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The costs for OPO-sponsored seminars where continuing education credits are given and where the attendee is on the OPO staff are allowable costs to the extent that they are patient care related, reasonable and necessary (proposed addition of §413.5(c)(14)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to codify existing policy that such seminar costs are allowable only when patient-care related, reasonable, and necessary; cross-references to §486.326(b) and §413.9 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑OPO attendees at OPO‑sponsored CE seminars are not allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by OPOs for OPO-sponsored seminars where continuing education credits are given and where the attendee is not on the OPO staff are not allowable costs (proposed §413.5(c)(14)(iii), consistent with §413.402(d)(2)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy mirrors existing requirements under §413.402(d)(2)(v); CMS will cross-reference this exclusion in amended sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff training and education generally allowable if reasonable and patient‑care related
rubrics_metrics.description: The costs of staff training and education are allowable, provided they are reasonable and related to patient care (PRM‑1, chapter 21; e.g., orientation and on-the-job training recognized as normal operating expenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training typically conducted within the provider's setting; outside instruction is allowable if required; must meet Medicare reasonable cost principles under §413.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider‑paid convenience items may be allowable if related to patient care
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of items provided to the employee for the convenience of the provider (such as provider‑paid educational courses, uniforms, and operating day care centers for employees' children) may be included in allowable costs to the extent they are reasonable and related to patient care (PRM‑1 ch.21 §2144.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are not necessarily classified as fringe benefits and can be included if they meet reasonableness and patient-care relatedness tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to maintain continuous safety and training programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers are required to maintain continuous safety initiatives and professional and employee training programs aimed at reducing the severity of incidents related to malpractice, general liability, and workers' compensation (PRM‑1 ch.21 §2162.7 D.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such programs are cited as a justification for recognizing training-related costs as allowable when aimed at patient-care risk reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel costs allowable only if patient‑care related and reasonable
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by providers in conjunction with employee travel are generally allowable to the extent that they are patient care related and reasonable. Travel costs incurred for non-patient care travel are not allowable; foreign travel requires clear substantiation of reasonableness and patient‑care relatedness (PRM‑1 ch.21 §2105.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers must document reasonableness and patient-care nexus to satisfy Medicare contractors; foreign travel is scrutinized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overnight travel for education: 50‑mile / 8‑hour clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Overnight travel costs incurred by a provider on behalf of employees or staff for patient-care related professional education should be considered allowable when the event is located more than 50 miles away from the employee's workplace and requires more than 8 hours of attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS frames this as reflecting standard business practices and widely recognized definitions of local travel; documentation should show distance and attendance duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize travel costs (economy/coach expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers are expected to minimize travel-related costs to professional education activities by selecting economy or coach class accommodations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS signals an expectation of cost‑conscious booking practices; unnecessary upgrades may render costs unreasonable/unallowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal use of provider vehicles not allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by providers related to employee personal use of provider vehicles are not allowable costs (section 1861(v)(8)(iii) and PRM‑1 ch.21 §2105.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG audits have found instances where personal-use vehicle costs were reported and deemed unallowable; such costs should be excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertainment/vacation travel expenses not allowable (cruises, resorts, events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entertainment and vacation travel expenses such as travel on cruises or to resorts or spas, or transportation to entertainment or sporting events, are not allowable costs regardless of whether incurred in connection with professional educational seminars or continuing education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cites Administrator decisions (e.g., McCurry's Home Health) that costs of cruises and similar entertainment are not 'common and accepted' or reasonable; only a narrow cost of the seminar itself might be allowable in limited facts, but entertainment elements are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education expenses for spouses/dependents not allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Education expenses for spouses or other dependents of providers of services, their employees or contractors are unrelated to patient care and not allowable (section 1861(v)(8)(v) of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if dependent attendance accompanies an educational event, those costs are deemed unrelated to patient care and must be excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meals for non‑personnel are unallowable
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of meals for other than provider personnel is unallowable because it is not related to patient care (PRM‑1 ch.21 §2105.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS is clarifying prior positions after OIG findings that some OPO overhead claimed meals benefited non‑OPO employees and were unallowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meals provided at educational events (including OPO seminars) not allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of meals and refreshments provided to attendees at educational events, including attendees of OPO‑sponsored seminars (with or without continuing education credits), are not allowable costs (proposed §413.5(c)(16)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS reverses prior, narrower positions and treats such meals as a benefit to attendees rather than a direct patient-care cost; alcohol excluded in prior guidance but CMS proposes broader disallowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee meals—unrecovered shared dining costs may be allowable in narrow circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Unrecovered costs for employee meals served from common menus in shared employee dining facilities are allowable if otherwise reasonable; excess costs for executive/management meals (separate dining, extra staff, upgraded menus) are not allowable (PRM‑1 ch.21 §2105.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS distinguishes between common-menu unrecovered costs (potentially allowable) versus special executive perks (unallowable). Documentation should show reasonableness and common-menu context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meals may be allowable when qualifying as fringe benefit or solely for provider benefit related to patient care
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers may claim reasonable unrecovered costs for employee meals when meals qualify as a fringe benefit related to patient care or are provided solely for the provider's benefit and related to patient care (PRM‑1 ch.21 §2145 and §2144.4E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: meals served to personnel who must remain on‑call on the premises during mealtime to provide patient care where the meal cost is not classified as a fringe benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providers must provide adequate, verifiable cost data and use approved cost finding methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicare regulations (42 CFR 413.24) require providers to provide adequate cost data based on financial and statistical records capable of verification by qualified auditors, and cost data must be based on an approved method of cost finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost reports must be accurate, sufficiently detailed, and auditable to support Medicare payments; failure may result in disallowances or audit adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct versus indirect costs (and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct costs are specifically identifiable and attributable to an individual patient, cost center, or department (examples: staff salaries dedicated to a department, medical supplies used in patient care). Indirect costs are not chargeable by actual usage and must be allocated by a statistical surrogate (examples: administration, rent, depreciation, utilities, housekeeping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct classification is critical because direct costs are assigned to cost centers while indirect costs are allocated; misclassification distorts reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation statistical basis must reflect cause‑and‑effect and resource consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The statistical basis used to allocate overhead must reflect the cause‑and‑effect relationship between the cost and the activities or services receiving the allocation and must demonstrate how costs incurred relate to the consumption of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended MCR statistical bases include square footage for facility costs, gross salaries for employee benefits, accumulated costs for A&G, and meals served for dietary; choose bases that proportionately distribute costs according to benefit received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include statistical costs that receive no benefit (remove purchased services from accumulated cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a statistical basis (such as accumulated cost) improperly includes costs that receive no benefit or resources, those costs must not be used to allocate cost to a department or cost center; providers must remove directly assigned purchased costs from the accumulated cost statistic (per MCR instructions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purchased services (e.g., organs purchased from OPOs, CAR‑T purchases) already include external entity overhead and must bypass step‑down allocation; including them inflates allocations and causes improper Medicare payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchased services are direct costs and must bypass step‑down allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchased services are reported as direct costs and must bypass the step-down allocation process because the purchase price already reflects the external entity's overhead and profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers should not include purchased-service costs in accumulated cost statistics used for A&G allocations; follow MCR instructions to remove such amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative Adjustment Method for accumulated cost corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Method to adjust allocation statistic: identify cost centers not to receive allocation by entering a negative one (-1) in the accumulated cost column or entering the total accumulated cost as a negative amount in the reconciliation column; partial exclusions are entered as negative amounts in reconciliation (proposed 413.24(d)(8)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Worksheet B‑1 reconciliation column to remove purchased service costs from the statistic; ensure entries properly offset to avoid double entries that confuse allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules on reconciliation and accumulated cost column entries when excluding cost centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost centers that are not to receive an allocation must not have entries in both the reconciliation and accumulated cost columns when the accumulated cost statistic is offset to zero; for partial allocations, report the excluded cost as a negative amount on the reconciliation line resulting in entries in both columns for that line (proposed 413.24(d)(8)(ii)(B)-(C)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow precise worksheet entry rules to ensure correct exclusion of costs and avoid improper allocation results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fragmenting/Componentizing A&G Method
rubrics_metrics.description: When a provider chooses to fragment (componentize) A&G costs, the provider must subscript the A&G cost center into two or more cost centers using accurate statistics to allocate its costs and ensure overhead costs are accurately assigned to departments benefiting from the services (proposed 413.24(d)(8)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create multiple A&G cost centers (e.g., HR, IT, facilities) and use different statistical bases for each to better reflect resource consumption and provide clearer documentation for auditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providers must not include statistical costs that cause improper distribution of overhead
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers must not include a statistical cost which does not relate to the allocation of A&G expenses when it causes an improper distribution of overhead (proposed 413.24(d)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will codify this to prevent inflated A&G allocations; examples include removal of high-dollar purchased organ costs from accumulated-cost statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to request change of cost finding method (90‑day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A provider that wishes to change its cost finding method must submit a request in writing to its Medicare contractor 90 days prior to the end of the cost reporting period to which the request applies; the contractor's determination will be furnished in writing and binding as of that date, and approved methods must be used for that and subsequent periods unless changed again by approval (PRM‑1 ch.23 §2312; proposed 413.24(d)(8)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers must follow this timeline and documentation requirement; contractors' approvals are binding and govern future reporting periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAH‑specific caution about improper allocation impacting reimbursement
rubrics_metrics.description: Because CAHs are reimbursed at 101 percent of reasonable costs, improper allocation of A&G costs (e.g., using accumulated cost without causal relationships) can shift costs and undesirably affect CAH reimbursement calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAHs should be especially careful to avoid allocating costs without demonstrable causal/beneficial relationships; consider fragmentation or negative adjustments where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator discretionary review of CMS reviewing official and hearing officer decisions (IOPOs/HCLs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CMS Administrator has discretionary authority to review a CMS reviewing official decision and contractor hearing officer decisions for reimbursement appeals for IOPOs and HCLs, either on request by a party or on the Administrator's own motion (proposed changes to §413.420(g) and related appeals provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes regulatory changes to codify Standing Order 2023‑1, provide clarity and consistency with other agency review processes, and allow IOPOs/HCLs to seek Administrator review resulting in a final Agency decision binding HHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming/applicable regulatory revisions to appeals provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revisions to §§405.1801(a) and 405.1803(d)(1)(ii) to reflect that Administrator review includes review described in §405.1834 as well as §405.1875, and to align appeals process language with the proposed Administrator discretionary review authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conforming edits will align the statutory/regulatory cross‑references so Administrator review is clearly part of the appeal pathway for affected providers.
